channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Crude Oil Futures Post Back-to Back Losses
item.description: Oil prices fell amid expectations that Saudi Arabia could soon restore some oil flows through its damaged East-West pipeline while shipping crude through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts for September 2026: Up to 4.50%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: The New Offensive Raising Oil Prices and Complicating Trump’s Iran War
item.description: WSJ’s Shelby Holliday explains how the Houthis pulled off a swift offensive that has sparked fighting and sent oil prices soaring.

item.title: Stellantis Could Face Strike Threat in Canada Over Factory Sale
item.description: The union representing more than 9,000 Stellantis employees in Canada said it could be in a strike position in the coming weeks unless the carmaker changes course on its plan to sell a Toronto-area factory to a defense firm.

item.title: Why the Bank of England Didn’t Follow the Fed in Raising Interest Rates
item.description: The U.K. central bank is monitoring for signs that higher energy costs are spilling over into everyday prices.

item.title: U.S. Probes Iran Link to Cyberattacks on Texas-Bound Energy Tankers
item.description: The vessels were attacked in the Strait of Gibraltar as they made their way to U.S. ports.

item.title: Carney Puts His Pivot Away From the U.S. to the Test
item.description: The Canadian leader is attempting the most dramatic reorientation of his country’s economy and alliances in almost 40 years.

item.title: EU Could Require Age Verification in Minors’ Social Media Restrictions
item.description: Under formally presented new rules, social networks could be required to use age verification tools to stop under 15s creating their own accounts, and children under 13 would be banned from accessing social media.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Has Another Option to Get Its Oil Out
item.description: A shuttle service that slips oil through the Strait of Hormuz now looks like the kingdom’s best fallback.

item.title: Iran’s Attempts to Get Around the Hormuz Blockade Are Hitting a Wall
item.description: While Saudi Arabia and others move goods overland, hundreds of truckers are trapped at Iran’s land borders, threatening its economy.

item.title: See How Jet Power Is Giving Russia the Edge in the Drone War
item.description: Jet drones are the latest innovation in robot combat over Ukraine.

item.title: Trump Says Allowing Canada to Become Associate Member of EU Could Be ‘Hostile Act’
item.description: The president threatened to either cut off trade or impose more tariffs on European countries.

item.title: Top Democrat Opposes Trump’s Planned Sale of Heavy Bombs to Israel
item.description: The administration has options to bypass the objection, but the move highlights a sensitive issue ahead of the midterms.

item.title: Harold Hamm’s Continental Resources Signs Preliminary Oil Deal in Venezuela
item.description: The company, led by one of President Trump’s closest allies in the U.S. oil industry, said it would explore one of Venezuela’s undeveloped oil fields.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthi Rebels Claim Shooting Down Saudi F-15 Jet Fighter
item.description: The claimed downing of the Saudi jet comes as the kingdom is squeezed by the Iran-backed rebels’ advance and attacks targeting its oil industry.

item.title: Debris Found in Yemen Suggests Saudi Arabia Fired Its First Chinese Missile
item.description: The body of what appeared to be a Dongfeng 15 was found in the desert.

item.title: EU Chief Backs Canada’s Push to Become Bloc’s First Associate Member
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s comments follow efforts by Canada’s Mark Carney to accelerate his country’s pivot to the bloc.

item.title: What Would Canada’s Associate Membership of the EU Look Like?
item.description: The title is entirely new and significant hurdles remain before it could become Canada’s official status.

item.title: Former Kosovo President Sentenced to 25 Years for War Crimes in Serbia Conflict
item.description: Hashim Thaci was convicted in one of the final verdicts in a series of landmark trials arising from the bloody dissolution of the former Yugoslavia.

item.title: Eurozone Industrial Production Fell at Start of Third Quarter
item.description: The data highlights the uneven nature of the region’s recovery as manufacturers contend with higher energy costs despite signs of improving demand.
